patch_description: Replace the placeholder circle configuration with a deterministic multi-start hill-climbing optimizer. The approach exploits the scale-invariance of the normalized objective (min triangle area / hull area): points are optimized freely, the score is computed as (smallest of the 286 triangle areas) / (convex hull area), and the final configuration is rescaled so the hull has unit area. Key design choices: (1) multiple deterministic seeds (regular 13-gon, jittered 13-gons, center+12-ring, random-in-disk) to escape poor local optima; (2) targeted moves that perturb vertices belonging to the currently worst (smallest) triangle, plus a reflection move across the opposite edge midpoint — a classic heuristic for max-min geometric problems; (3) geometrically decaying step size for coarse-to-fine convergence; (4) a hard wall-clock deadline so evaluation time stays bounded; (5) a pure-Python convex hull (monotone chain) and vectorized numpy triangle-area computation over all C(13,3)=286 triples for speed. A fixed RNG seed guarantees reproducibility, and a graceful fallback keeps the function valid even if numpy is unavailable.
